# ACT UP Oral History Project -- domain lexicon.
#
# Serves two purposes at once, deliberately:
#   1. Scored metric. `score` counts occurrences of each term in the cleaned truth
#      (`expected`) and in the hypothesis (`found`). Terms with expected == 0 for a
#      given interview are skipped in the recall figure, so corpus-wide entries below
#      cost nothing when scoring a single transcript.
#   2. Decoder prompt. The same list seeds `set_initial_prompt`, which is the
#      highest-leverage fix for exactly the failures this metric detects.
#
# Keep the prompt-facing selection under ~200 tokens: the initial prompt consumes
# decoder context, and an over-stuffed one degrades what it was meant to help.
#
# Format: one term per line. `#` comments and blank lines ignored. Matching is done
# on the normalised token stream, so casing and punctuation here are for human
# readability only -- write terms the way a person would.

# -- The core terms ----------------------------------------------------------
# `AIDS` was missing until interview 074 made the omission obvious: it is the
# single most searched word in the archive and appears in every transcript.
# Worth stating plainly --- a lexicon is only as good as its most boring entries.
AIDS
HIV
ACT UP
